_comment: Rotation for the weekly mutation run. ONE slice per week, picked by ISO week
number modulo the length of `slices`. A slice is a list of files, not a target,
because whole targets do not fit: measured on 2026-08-18, mutation density is
about ONE MUTANT PER 6 LINES and each mutant costs one test-suite run (~16s).
Whole-target runtimes at that rate: RunnerCore ~1h10m, Worker ~4h11m,
`testArgs` is the command each mutant is graded with. Keep it as narrow as
possible while still COVERING the sliced files -- a mutant whose covering test
is not run survives, and reads as a hole that does not exist.
COVERAGE IS DELIBERATELY PARTIAL. The bulk of APIServer (94k LOC of Vapor
wiring) is not in the rotation and is not intended to be; it is covered by
APITests and the guard scripts. Slices name what is worth mutating, and the
workflow logs what it skipped rather than implying the tree is covered.

slices.name: RunnerCore — grading core
slices.why: Compiled natively AND to wasm from one source; pinned by Tests/Fixtures/output-contract.json. A survivor here means the two graders can drift unnoticed.

slices.name: RunnerCore — notebook extraction
slices.why: extractPython/extractR/extractLua marker handling; a silent extraction change mis-grades every notebook submission.

slices.name: Core — assignment language dispatch
slices.why: Every language-specific path dispatches on the declared value; the multi-language arc's defects all descended from getting this wrong.

slices.name: Core — pattern families and notebook checks
slices.why: Renders the generated tests students are graded by. A wrong literal or comparison is invisible until a student disputes a mark.

slices.name: Worker — submission normalization
slices.why: Pre-processes uploads before the shell scripts see them; a mistake here changes what every test in the job runs against.

slices.name: Worker — job lifecycle
slices.why: Claim, run, report. A survivor can mean a job is silently dropped or double-claimed.
